what_happened: In job bzw6, the user corrected Athena's first reading of a request about writing landing records to the athena/records branch. The user gave four decisions from the planner's last critique. (1) The remote is the source of truth: build the records commit on the remote tip, push with a lease on that tip, move the local ref only after the push succeeds, and on rejection fetch, rebuild and retry a bounded number of times. A local ref that is ahead or diverged is reset to the remote first. (2) If the host merged but land cannot confirm the merge, write no landing record and warn with the intent, leaving repair to the later reconcile job. (3) The drain.rs caller of land_pr is covered the same way. (4) An error for a commit with no landing or verification names its sha and says it lies between the remote base and the PR head. The correction came before work went on. The event does not say what the first reading wrote.
cause: The reading is built from the request text alone. The critique of an earlier plan holds recovery and end-state decisions: which side is the source of truth, what happens on a push race, what to do when a merge cannot be confirmed, and which other callers are affected. Nothing carries those findings into the reading, and nothing makes the reading state them as criteria. The user therefore had to restate them. This is the same gap as in ywyz: follow-up readings do not take in what the earlier stage already decided.
prevention: When a job's request follows a planning critique or an earlier attempt, the reading stage must be given that critique's findings and decisions. It must list each one as a criterion or as an explicit exclusion, and the accepted reading must show that mapping. A reading that leaves out an open finding is not accepted. The same check would cover the earlier case, where the retry's kept work and rules were left out.
proposed_request: Make the reading stage take in the prior critique or earlier-attempt result for a follow-up or retry job. Done when: (1) the reading input includes the findings and decisions of the last critique or attempt for the same work; (2) the accepted reading maps each finding to a criterion or to a stated exclusion with a reason; (3) a reading that leaves any finding unmapped is returned for revision before the work starts; (4) a test with a fixture critique that has four decisions shows an unmapped one is caught and a fully mapped reading passes; (5) a CHANGELOG entry is added.
